title: DriveMind: Mind-Evolving Belief Tracking for Closed-Loop Autonomous Driving

body: Recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can perceive a traffic scene, reason about it, and propose a driving action within a single model. However, existing MLLM-based drivers reason from scratch at each frame and commit to a single explanation, discarding earlier hypotheses about the scene. When the scene is ambiguous, the agent locks in on the wrong interpretation and acts on it before evidence accumulates. In this paper, we propose DriveMind, an MLLM-based driving framework that keeps several hypotheses about the scene alive at the same time and updates their weights as new frames arrive. Inspired by particle filtering, DriveMind propagates each hypothesis through a VLM, scores it against the current observation, and resamples to maintain diversity. On Bench2Drive, adding belief tracking to the same driving pipeline improves the Driving Score (DS) from 68.50 to 81.37 and the Success Rate (SR) from 41.36% to 54.09%. The largest gains occur on ambiguous scenarios such as unsignalized intersections (+20.0 DS) and oncoming-traffic interactions (+20.5 DS). Beyond the overall metrics, DriveMind also improves fine-grained interactive driving abilities such as merging, emergency braking, and give-way.
summaryZh: DriveMind：用于闭环自动驾驶的思维进化信念跟踪。最近的多模态大语言模型（MLLM）可以感知交通场景，对其进行推理，并在单个模型中提出驾驶动作。然而，现有的基于 MLLM 的驱动程序在每一帧上都从头开始推理，并致力于单一解释，放弃了早期关于场景的假设。
